current.text: His wrist is healthy again and he is expected to be fine coming into the season.
Experts say expecting last season's injuries to repeat would be a mistake, but he still has to prove he can stay healthy. It is too early to call him injury prone.
He is a projected starter at the three, next to Shai, Cason Wallace, Chet Holmgren and Isaiah Hartenstein.
OKC lost Lu Dort, Aaron Wiggins and Isaiah Joe. Apart from Alex Caruso, he is the only wing left who can guard bigger forwards.
Those departures open up usage, and the team may lean more on offense with SGA, Ajay Mitchell and Williams together.
The team may push him to shoot more threes, for example seven in a game, even if it costs some efficiency. OKC needs more three-point volume from its core players.
Experts agree the market dropped him too far after last season's injuries. He now goes around pick 45, at the back end of his value.

Experts differ a little on his price. The newest call ranks him steadily in the 30 to 40 range and takes him in round three without hesitation. Others call the 40s a fine range and say 29 USD in an auction mock was too high.
OKC is projected for about 57 to 62 wins and a top-two seed in the West.
OKC has 13 back-to-backs, the league minimum.
The OKC schedule is pretty good for a March 28 season end.

durable.text: Last season he had wrist surgery that cost him the start of the season, then several hamstring strains after he returned.
Many of last season's games came at about 20 minutes while he recovered. Only about 20 were full-speed games.
He takes very few threes. When they do not go in, he stops taking them.
His stats swing a lot from year to year.
His high block, rebound and FG% rates came when he played center. On a healthy team he plays the three.
He is an elite defender who can guard positions one through five, described as All-NBA and All-Defense caliber.
Assists and steals are his best categories, both well above other forwards. No category is weak.

note: He costs about 19.4 USD on both Yahoo and ESPN, with values of 25 and 20 USD and ranks of 35 to 37. He went for 35 USD in our league last season. Experts call him a round three to four player the market dropped too far, so 20 to 25 USD looks like a good buy, but they see 29 USD as too high. Big assists and steals for a forward and no weak category make him fit any build. Early in the season, check that his hamstring holds up, that he plays a full starter's minutes, and whether OKC really gets him to shoot more threes.
